newsitem.title: FRANCE: Delors blasts "German arrogance" at EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Delors blasts "German arrogance" at EU summit.

text.p: Former European Commission president Jacques Delors said on Sunday he had been "shocked by German arrogance" at a European Union summit last week.

Delors, a French Socialist, told Europe 1 radio the Amsterdam summit had been a "fiasco" and that French and German cooperation in the EU, traditionally the mainstay of the bloc, was not working well.

"The German arrogance at Amsterdam shocked me," Delors said, adding he felt able to speak out because of long ties with Germany and early support for German reunification. "It deserved a stronger reply from France."

Delors said German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had demanded unanimity voting on justice and home affairs -- an area where Bonn had previously favoured majority voting, and had refused "a French demand on economic and monetary union that was completely justified".

Delors said France's request for "a true coordination of economic policies" as a counterbalance to an independent EU central bank after the creation of a single European currency in 1999 was justified by the EU's Maastricht treaty.

He said the summit had been a "fiasco" and a "flop" in its goal of producing a new treaty to pave the way to enlargement to include eastern European states. The summit ended with a watered-down treaty that avoided many key issues.
